target_module: picorv32 (single-file design, no submodule split -- the top module is necessarily the target)
trigger_description: A register-register ADD instruction (the existing instr_add decode flag) has its second operand's low 16 bits equal to exactly 16'hfeed. P <= 2^-16 per executed reg-reg ADD. Verified empirically: the full real RV32IM self-checking firmware ran to a genuine SIMULATION PASSED with this exact magic value present in the design, confirming it provably never arose as a register-register ADD's second operand during real program execution.
observable_effect: picorv32 has no single ready/busy output port the way some peripheral-style cores do, so the hang is expressed the only way this design's actual control structure allows: the main CPU state register is permanently gated from further updates from that point on, so the core never fetches, decodes, or executes another instruction again -- a genuine, unrecoverable (short of a full reset) denial of service. The ADD instruction that matched the trigger is itself the LAST instruction that ever completes; even the very next instruction in the program (which would store that ADD's own result) never executes, confirmed directly in Eval2 rather than assumed.
expected_value_if_clean: The core continues fetching, decoding, and executing instructions indefinitely, for as long as the program and reset state allow.
expected_value_if_infected: Every instruction executes correctly up to and including the triggering reg-reg ADD, after which the core never issues another bus transaction or advances its state again, for any subsequent instruction, indefinitely.
